Asymmetric C atalysis
Rhodium-Catalyzed Dynamic Kinetic [4+2] Cycloaddition of Allene-
1,3-Dienes
Yulin Han
+
, Anni Qin
+
, Qian Zhang, Xue Zhang,* Hui Qian,* and Shengming Ma*
In memory of Prof. Jirō Tsuji
Abstract: Rh-catalyzed dynamic kinetic intramolecular
[4+2] cycloaddition reaction of 1,3-disubstituted allene-
1,3-dienes afforded cis-fused [4.3.0]bicyclic products
with an excellent chemo-, diastereo-, and enantio-
selectivity. Many synthetically useful functional groups
are tolerated. The synthetic utility has been demon-
strated. Based on the careful experimental studies, a
mechanism involving the rapid racemization of the
allene moiety in the starting materials has been
proposed.
Introduction
Allenes are versatile building blocks
[1]
and have been
becoming an integral part in organic synthesis due to their
unique axial chirality
[2]
and chemical properties.
[3]
Although
some examples of classic kinetic resolution (KR) with the
theoretic maximum yield of 50 % have been reported
(Scheme 1a),
[4]
catalytic dynamic kinetic transformations
involving the racemization of allenes have not been well
established (Scheme 1b).
[5–8]
Only a few examples of catalytic
allene racemization have been reported.
[9]
Thus, establishing
overall processes combining both the rapid racemization and
excellent enantioselective conversions are still of high
interest. Herein, we wish to report the first example of
rhodium-catalyzed dynamic kinetic transformation of race-
mic allene-1,3-dienes, i.e., the asymmetric [4+2] cycloaddi-
tion of allene-1,3-dienes
[10]
with Malphos
[11]
as the chiral
ligand, affording cis-fused [4.3.0]bicyclic products, which are
important skeletons in bioactive compounds
[12]
(Scheme 1d).
It should be noted that three chiral centers have been
generated at the same time with an excellent enantio- and
diastereoselectivity (Scheme 1c).

diverse two-carbon bridges L8–L12 could not give better
results. We also investigated other biarylphosphine ligands.
(S)-SEGphos L13, (R)-Tol-BINAP (L14, BINAP = 1.1’-
Binaphthyl-2.2’-diphemyl phosphine), (R)-Ph-Garphos L15
and Duanphos L17 were inefficient for this reaction. (R,R)-
DACH-Ph Trost Ligand (L16, DACH = diaminocyclohex-

2 a, however, the enantioselectivity is very low. Mono-
phosphine ligands L18–L20 afforded (3aR,5S,7aR,Z)-2 a in
an essentially racemic form. Based on these results of ligand
screening, Malphos is the most efficient ligand. It may be
due to its perfect bite angle (86.1 ° ) as compared with those
of L6 (83.6 ° ) and L9 (83.2 ° ), L1 (123 ° ), L11 (96 ° ), and L16
(125 ° ).

69 % yield of product could be obtained with 86 % ee
(Entry 4). Lower yields and enantioselectivity of (3aR,5-
S,7aR,Z)-2 a was obtained when the reaction was performed
in MeOH and HFIP (hexafluoroisopropanol) under other-
wise identical conditions (Entries 5 and 6).

To demonstrate the practicality of this protocol, 1.0785 g
of (2E,4E)-1 a was submitted to the standard reaction

bicylic product (3aR,5S,7aR,Z)-2 a can be transformed into

afforded the single epoxide 4 a with an excellent diastereose-
lectivity. The absolute configurations of the chiral centers in

C onclusion
In conclusion, we have developed the Rh-catalyzed dynamic
kinetic intramolecular [4+2]-cycloaddition reaction of 1,3-
disubstituted allene-dienes to afford cis-fused [4.3.0]bicyclic
products generating three chiral centers in one shot with an
excellent diastereoselectivity and enantioselectivity by ap-
plying Malphos as the chiral ligand. The reaction exhibits
good substrate scope and functional group compatibility.
The synthetic potential of the products for the asymmetric
syntheses of other useful building blocks has also been
demonstrated. Mechanistic studies demonstrated the nature
